airport: Airports show long, straight runways with distinct markings, connected to large terminal buildings, hangars, and aircraft parking stands. They differ from parking lots by having runways and aircraft rather than vehicle rows; ports show water, docks, and ships rather than aviation facilities; resorts show hotel buildings and pools rather than airport infrastructure.
bareland: Bare land appears as exposed soil or rock surfaces with minimal vegetation, showing smooth to uneven textures and light brown tones. It contrasts with desert by lacking sand dune formations and being less uniformly sandy; viaducts show elevated road structures rather than bare soil; forests show dense tree cover rather than exposed ground.
baseballfield: Baseball fields show diamond-shaped infields with visible pitcher's mound, baselines, and outfield grass. They differ from stadiums by being open fields without large surrounding stands; playgrounds show recreational equipment rather than sports diamond; parks have irregular wooded areas and paths rather than sports fields.
beach: Beaches appear as sandy or pebbly shorelines along water bodies, with light colors and wave patterns. They contrast with ports by having natural sand rather than docks and ships; deserts show inland sandy areas without water adjacency; ponds are small water bodies without sandy shorelines.
bridge: Bridges show elevated roadway or railway structures spanning over water or valleys, with visible pillars, deck, and approach ramps. They differ from viaducts by spanning over water rather than land; ports show waterfront docks rather than crossing structures; rivers show water channels without bridges.
center: Centers are characterized by high-density commercial buildings, large plazas, and major public structures with dense street networks. They contrast with stadiums by having mixed-use towers rather than sports arenas; squares show paved public plazas rather than dense commercial blocks; churches show religious architecture rather than commercial buildings.
church: Churches show distinctive religious architecture with prominent spires, steeples, or domes, often with a central nave. They differ from squares by having religious buildings rather than public plazas; centers show dense commercial blocks rather than churches; playgrounds show recreational areas rather than religious structures.
commercial: Commercial areas show dense retail and office buildings with large parking lots, wide streets, and visible storefronts. They contrast with squares by having retail blocks rather than public plazas; parking lots show vehicle storage without buildings; centers have more civic and public buildings rather than retail.
denseresidential: Dense residential features tightly packed housing units with small yards, narrow streets, and uniform block patterns. It differs from medium residential by having smaller lot sizes; sparse residential shows wider spacing and more vegetation; squares show paved public plazas rather than housing blocks.
desert: Deserts show vast, barren landscapes with sand dunes, rocky outcrops, and sparse dry vegetation. They contrast with bare land by having dune formations and being less disturbed; mountains show elevated rocky peaks; beaches show coastal sandy areas adjacent to water.
farmland: Farmland appears as large, open agricultural fields with uniform crop rows, regular field boundaries, and occasional irrigation. It differs from meadow by having organized crop rows rather than natural grassland; ponds show small water bodies within fields; industrial areas show factories and storage rather than crops.
forest: Forests show dense tree canopy with dark green textures, irregular edges, and no visible ground. They contrast with mountains by having tree cover rather than exposed rock; ponds show water features rather than canopy; sparse residential shows houses and lawns rather than dense tree cover.
industrial: Industrial areas feature large warehouses, factories, smokestacks, and extensive parking lots with regular blocky layouts. They differ from storage tanks by having buildings and smokestacks rather than circular metallic containers; railway stations show tracks and passenger buildings rather than industrial structures; farmland shows agricultural fields rather than factories.
meadow: Meadows show open, grassy areas with smooth, uniform texture, often with scattered trees, and no field lines. They contrast with farmland by lacking organized crop rows; baseball fields have sports markings and infield dirt; bare land shows exposed soil without grass cover.
mediumresidential: Medium residential shows moderately sized houses on medium lots with visible yards, driveways, and tree-lined streets. It differs from dense residential by having larger lots; sparse residential shows widely spaced houses with large wooded lots; resorts show hotel buildings and pools rather than residential neighborhoods.
mountain: Mountains show elevated, rugged terrain with steep slopes, rocky outcrops, and shadow patterns. They contrast with forests by having exposed rock and elevation changes; deserts show sand dunes rather than rocky peaks; bare land lacks dramatic elevation and ridges.
park: Parks show green open spaces with trees, walking paths, ponds, and recreational areas, often irregular in shape. They differ from squares by being green spaces with grass rather than paved plazas; ponds are water features within parks; playgrounds show recreational equipment rather than park paths.
parking: Parking lots appear as flat, paved areas with rows of vehicles, clear lane markings, and entrance points. They differ from airports by having no runways or aircraft; industrial areas have buildings alongside parking; ports show water, docks, and ships rather than parked vehicles.
playground: Playgrounds show recreational areas with equipment like slides and swings, often within parks or schools. They differ from stadiums by being smaller recreational zones without large stands; schools have multiple buildings and larger campuses; parks are larger green areas with paths and trees.
pond: Ponds appear as small, circular or irregular water bodies with calm surfaces, often surrounded by vegetation. They contrast with forests by having water rather than tree cover; farmland shows crop fields rather than water features; beaches show shoreline rather than enclosed water bodies.
port: Ports show waterfront areas with docks, piers, ships, cranes, and large storage areas adjacent to water. They differ from beaches by having industrial infrastructure rather than natural sand; resorts show hotels and pools rather than port facilities; parking lots show vehicles rather than ships.
railwaystation: Railway stations show tracks, platforms, passenger buildings, and surrounding parking lots. They contrast with industrial areas by having passenger buildings and platforms rather than factories; viaducts show elevated rail structures rather than ground-level stations; airports have runways and terminals rather than train tracks.
resort: Resorts show hotel buildings, pools, tennis courts, and landscaped grounds, often near beaches. They differ from ports by having recreational facilities rather than docks and ships; parks have natural vegetation rather than hotel buildings; beaches show natural sand without built resort infrastructure.
river: Rivers appear as narrow, sinuous, dark water channels with flowing patterns and riparian vegetation. They contrast with ponds by being elongated flowing water rather than still water bodies; bridges are structures spanning across rivers; farmland shows crop fields rather than water channels.
school: Schools show campus layouts with classroom buildings, playgrounds, sports fields, and surrounding parking lots. They differ from squares by having educational facilities rather than public plazas; playgrounds show recreational areas rather than campus buildings; parks show natural vegetation rather than school facilities.
sparseresidential: Sparse residential shows widely separated houses surrounded by large vegetated lots, with low building density. It contrasts with medium residential by having larger lot sizes; forests show tree cover without houses; ponds are small water features within residential areas.
square: Squares show paved public plazas with geometric layouts, central monuments or fountains, and surrounding buildings. They differ from parks by being paved with minimal grass; commercial areas have retail buildings rather than open plazas; schools have campus buildings rather than public gathering spaces.
stadium: Stadiums show large sports venues with oval or rectangular shape, tiered seating, and surrounding parking. They contrast with playgrounds by having enclosed stands and much larger scale; baseball fields are open fields without stadium structures; centers show commercial towers rather than sports venues.
storagetanks: Storage tanks appear as large circular metallic containers with domed or flat roofs, arranged in industrial clusters. They differ from industrial areas by being rows of tanks rather than factories; ports show waterfront docks rather than tank farms; farmland shows agricultural fields rather than metallic containers.
viaduct: Viaducts show elevated road or rail structures with long continuous sections and multiple supports, often crossing over land. They differ from bridges by spanning over land rather than water; railway stations are ground-level with tracks rather than elevated structures; bare land shows exposed soil without any built infrastructure.
